entries.body:
The protocol Balancer suffered a major exploit that drained over $110 million across several blockchains, including Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Sonic. Attackers exploited faulty access control in the manageUserBalance function of Balancer's v2 , enabling unauthorized internal withdrawals. The stolen tokens included 6,850 osETH, 6,590 wETH, and 4,260 wstETH, later consolidated into new wallets likely for laundering.

The exploit also impacted protocols like Beets Finance, which lost around $3 million. Balancer's BAL token dropped over 10% following the theft.

This was Balancer's third major security incident since 2020, despite prior by OpenZeppelin and Trail of Bits.

entries.body:
The Garden bitcoin suffered a roughly $11 million loss after one of its solvers was compromised. These solvers essentially act as market makers for the protocol. Some blockchain sleuths have questioned whether the affected solver, which Garden described as a separate entity, may actually be operated by the same team as Garden.

There wasn't much sympathy to be had for Garden after this exploit. The protocol had recently announced hitting a milestone of bridging more than $2 billion in assets, but the celebration was criticized after zachxbt pointed out that a substantial portion of the bridged funds were proceeds of crimes being laundered to evade detection and recovery.

An attacker apparently obtained access to a victim's , enabling them to drain $21 million in various crypto assets. The attacker quickly bridged the stolen funds to ETH, then bounced through various addresses in hopes of disguising their origin and making the funds more challenging to recover.

Some originally feared that the theft was enabled by an exploit on Hyperliquid itself, shortly after another Hyperliquid-based project was compromised, but the theft appears to have been a key leak rather than an exploit on the protocol.

entries.body:
In their third major hack in two years, the Abracadabra lending project lost $1.8 million of their Magic Internet Money . An attacker took advantage of a bug in the project to borrow more than their provided collateral would normally allow. The attack was funded via Tornado Cash, and the exploiter then swapped the stolen tokens for ETH and laundered them back through Tornado.

The project disclosed the theft, describing the exploit as affecting "some deprecated contracts". They downplayed the theft, saying they'd bought back the stolen assets using treasury funds.

Abracadabra previously suffered a $13 million theft in March 2025, and a $6.5 million theft in January 2024.

Exploiters drained $782,000 in crypto assets from two markets on the Hyperdrive lending protocol, which is built on the Hyperliquid layer-1 blockchain. The attacker apparently took advantage of a security flaw in one of the project's smart contracts to drain the funds.

Hyperdrive paused all markets while investigating the vulnerability, and patched the bug. They also compensated those who had lost money in the exploit.

Crypto sleuth zachxbt observed $21 million in "suspicious outflows" from SBI Crypto, a crypto subsidiary of the Japanese SBI Group. The money was quickly laundered through instant exchanges and Tornado Cash, in ways zachxbt observed were similar to tactics of North Korean crypto thieves.

SBI Crypto has not made any public statements addressing the apparent theft.

entries.title: Griffin AI exploited for $3 million one day after launch

image.alt: An illustration of a predatory bird, followed by "Griffin AI", all in blue-green gradient
image.caption: Griffin AI logo

links.archiveTweetAlt:
This is an incredibly difficult day, and I want to start by offering my deepest, most sincere apologies to the entire Griffin AI community. Most importantly:  this malicious attack does not impact the long-term outlook of Griffin AI.

I've been working in crypto for 9 years, and this security incident is still shocking to me. I need to take full responsibility: a misconfigured layer Zero (cross-chain messaging) set-up and compromised key enabled the hacker to exploit the bridge to Binance Smart Chain. This happened on my watch. As CEO, it is my responsibility to enforce our security procedures on all and every team member day in and day out. 

I am truly sorry for the uncertainty, disruption and loss this has caused on you. We are working day and night to fix this and have a clear plan of how to make it happen.  

Details can be found in the post from 
@Griffin_AI
  X account. Here are the key points:

- The Breach: An attacker exploited a cross-chain endpoint to mint 5B fake $GAIN tokens on the BSC network. They managed to sell roughly 2.8% of these fake tokens for an estimated USD $3 million.

- Immediate Actions: We secured the cross-chain connection, notified all exchanges to halt $GAIN deposits/withdrawals/trading, shut down the Pancakeswap LP, and engaged law enforcement.

- The Path Forward: We have brought on independent security and development companies for a full post-mortem. Together with them, we are preparing for an immediate migration to a new, fully audited token. We will restore legitimate balances for our community based on pre-hack snapshots.

Your trust is everything, and we know the work required to earn it back is substantial. The entire team is mobilized, committed, and focused on one goal: restoring balances and relaunching GAIN secured with the hard lessons learned from this attack. 

We will share the full migration plan and timeline very soon. We are confident we will overcome this disruption and emerge as community even stronger than before. 

Finally, I am grateful to all of you for your support and patience. Seeing so many in our community fighting and rooting for us has given us strength. Thank you for being there for us and thank you to the wider crypto community for pulling together to help. We won't let you down. 
Tweeted at Sep 25

Update on the $GAIN Token Hack
•  Our Ethereum token is safe and unaffected.
•  The attacker deployed the malicious peer contract on the Ethereum network exploiting cross-chain endpoint and minting ~5B fake $GAIN tokens on Binance Smart Chain.
•  The hacker sold ~2.8% of the minted fake token for estimated USD3m.
•  Initial investigation shows no evidence of insider criminal behaviour but the indication that one of the private keys was compromised.

Immediate action we took: 
•  We disabled our cross-chain connection to prevent further unauthorized minting via the bridge.
•  Exchanges notified to halt deposits, withdrawals, and trading of $GAIN on BSC.
•  Liquidity pool on Pancakeswap shut down.
•  Law enforcement notified.

Current status:
 We have engaged an independent security firm and preparing a new token and distribution based on snapshots to restore legitimate balances.

Further details are coming as we finalize the action plan. 
Tweeted at 11:00 AM · Sep 25, 2025

entries.body:
One day after Griffin AI launched its GAIN token on Binance Alpha, an attacker 5 billion fake GAIN tokens on the Ethereum blockchain, then exploited a cross-chain endpoint to trick the to the Binance chain into recognizing them as the real thing. The attacker was only able to sell a small fraction of their tokens, but they made off with approximately $3 million as the token plunged in price. According to CEO Oliver Feldmeier, the exploit was enabled by "a misconfigured layer Zero (cross-chain messaging) set-up and compromised key".

Griffin AI promises to allow customers to "build, deploy, and scale autonomous AI agents for crypto finance". These are essentially AI-powered bots that perform various functions — some of Griffin's advertised examples include a "robo-adviser" to provide "tailored investment strategies", and bots to do arbitrage trading or manage staked assets.

entries.body:
An attacker exploited for SFUND, the token issued by the Seedify launchpad and incubator. It appears the exploiter has profited around $1.7 million from the theft. Seedify issued a statement announcing the theft, and said the bridge that were exploited had been deployed for three years. The SFUND token crashed in price by around 80% before recovering somewhat.

Seedify has been a launchpad for blockchain games, NFT projects, and other web3 products. The team recently has embraced "vibe coding" — a practice in which people rely heavily on AI to generate code.

The "AI-powered web3 social platform" UXLINK was exploited by an attacker that gained control of the project's , then billions of the project's UXLINK token. Though the tokens were worth hundreds of millions of dollars on paper, low liquidity and a crashing token price means the attacker cashed out around $28 million.

Shortly after the hack, the attacker apparently approved a phishing contract, perhaps in their rush to swap tokens before the price crashed further or before exchanges could freeze the tokens. Around 542 million of the UXLINK tokens were sent to a phishing address as a result, though it doesn't appear the phishing wallet has been able to sell the tokens.

entries.body:
A for Shibarium, the network for the Shiba Inu project, was exploited for approximately $2.4 million in funds. The attacker bought 4.6 million BONE tokens (the governance token for Shibarium) using a , then used compromised validator signing keys to take control of the majority of validator power. Then, they used that control to drain around 225 ETH and 92.6 billion SHIB, together priced at around $2.4 million at the time of the theft.

The project has paused staking on the network, freezing the BONE tokens borrowed by the attacker, which may limit the attacker's profits.
